newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SPT SHARES DIVE BUT DEALERS SEE REBOUND.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SPT SHARES DIVE BUT DEALERS SEE REBOUND.

text.p: Shares in SPT Telecom a.s. the most heavily capitalised Czech company, fell sharply at mid-session driven by general pessimism about Czech equities rather than poor company fundamentals, dealers said.
At 1100 GMT, SPT was down 191 crowns, 5.8 percent to 3,054.
Dealers said that in contrast to falls from other major issues, SPT was probably the victim of bearish sentiment, especially from abroad, about the Czech economy as a whole .
"From my viewpoint, I think SPT is still the most attractive stock here....SPT from a longterm point of view is a very attractive stock," said ING Baring's Radim Bajgar.
For the first quarter, SPT posted higher operating profits of 2.73 billion crowns versus 2.3 billion in the first three months of 1996.
Net and pre-tax profits were slightly down on the first quarter of the year before but analysts said the figures obscured the strength SPT's fundamentals because of higher depreciation costs.

Bajgar said SPT's decline on Tuesday was probably explained by the continued mood of pessimism among foreign investors about the Czech Republic's macro-economic fundamentals and the poor reputation of the Czech capital markets.
Foreign investors mainly trade in the major issues. SPT accounts for 21 percent of the PX50's total capitalisation.
